title: Reservoir-led autoscale and throttle orchestration for GPU lanes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated reserve capacity but we still observe tail latency spikes and throughput degeneration when 'noisy' tenants burst. Current lane-level autoscale reacts too late or conflicts with short-lived burst isolation, causing broken SLAs and opaque billing effects.

Objectives: 1) Provide enforceable per-tenant throughput contracts (steady-state and burst window) that map to customer reservations; 2) Implement an autoscale orchestration that consumes and refills a central reservoir of burst tokens instead of unbounded burst allocation; 3) Make noisy-neighbor mitigation predictable (soft-throttle first, preemptive fair-eviction as last resort) and observable in the Console.

High-level solution: introduce a Reservoir Quota Adapter (RQA) in the control plane: a lightweight token reservoir per-physical-pool that mediates short-term burst capacity. Each tenant lane has a steady throughput bucket (guarantee) and a burst apron that draws tokens from the pool. The Autoscale Controller consults RQA when expanding lane allocations above steady guarantees. When reservoir is low, the controller applies progressive backpressure via throttling, KV-cache isolation heuristics, and reduced batch sizes before triggering cross-tenant preemption.

Key enforcement points: (a) Admission: API router checks steady vs requested throughput and annotates request with reservation token; (b) Agent-level enforcement: GPU agent implements a local token check and a cooperative pacing loop to honor throttle decisions; (c) Scheduler: autoscale and preemption decisions are scored by a fairness function (age, SLA, historical consumption) and executed with two-phase rollbacks to ensure graceful degradation.

Design trade-offs: Reservoir token model is conservative and prevents noisy tenants from consuming long-term capacity but may reduce short-burst throughput for highly spiky workloads. We intentionally prefer predictable degradation over unpredictable tail latency. To mitigate customer surprise, the Console will show reservoir utilization forecasts and a simulation mode for their reservation settings.

Testing & validation: unit + integration tests around token accounting, a simulator that replays 30 days of production traces to validate failover behavior, and a canary across one dedicated region (5% lanes). Failure modes to test: clock skew, control-plane partition, token double-counting, race on preemption, and agent crash during backfill.
acceptance_criteria: Reservoir Quota Adapter implemented in control plane and exposes metrics (tokens_total, tokens_available, tokens_consumed) to Console
Autoscale Controller consults RQA for any scale-up that would exceed lane steady guarantees
GPU agent enforces soft-throttle policy and exposes agent-level throttle events to tracing
Noisy neighbor incidents (defined by >30% degradation to other lanes' p95) are reduced by >=50% in canary compared to baseline
Console displays per-tenant steady_vs_burst utilization and a simulation tool for reservation sizing
Rollout path documented and automated roll-back within 15 minutes in case of regressions

risks: Control-plane token store becomes single point of contention under heavy scale-up events
Customers with very spiky, low-latency workloads may see increased tail latency when reservoir is exhausted
Complexity of two-phase preemption could lead to transient overcommit if rollback is slow
Metrics misinterpretation could trigger unnecessary support tickets if Console wording is unclear
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Add RQA service and gRPC API; instrument metrics and synthetic load tests
Phase 2: Integrate with Autoscale Controller and implement consult-before-scale semantics
Phase 3: Agent-level token checks and soft-throttle loop (cooperative pacing based on batch size and kv-cache eviction)
Phase 4: Preemption implementation with scoring, graceful handoff, and rollback path
Phase 5: Console features (utilization, simulation) and run canary + soak tests
rollout_plan: Canary 5% lanes in us-west-2, monitor p50/p95/p99 and reservoir depletion events
If stable for 72h (no more than 5% regressions in SLOs), increment to 25% lanes across two regions
Run 7-day soak with customer opt-in and a feature-flag for simulation UI
Full rollout contingent on pass criteria and post-mortem of canary incidents
metrics: p50, p95, p99 latency per-tenant and per-lane
scale-up requests denied due to reservoir exhaustion
number of soft-throttle events and duration
